# Process evidence contract v5

#2236 owns the pure parser and this contract. The independently authored conformance component owns the complete positive fixture, original22 controls, six additional false-green regressions and collector provenance controls. Its registration/acceptance is mandatory. #2234 owns execution and collection. No component or source combination may be published while these dependencies, independent review or real runtime gates remain unresolved.

Run the parser as `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 .github/scripts/verify_api_process_failure.py ARTIFACT_DIRECTORY`. Rejection is a nonzero exit/exception. Synthetic fixture success is not Go/PostgreSQL acceptance.

## Artifact provenance

The trusted producer is the independently reviewed #2234 workflow/controller at the exact source head recorded in `source.txt`. The official Go1.23.12 executable and postgres:17 container run only isolated test data. A keeper retains the container namespace after PostgreSQL exits. The controller records actual postmaster/logger PID and `/proc` start ticks, verifies parent ownership, uses pg_ctl fast stop, observes the same logger absent, archives while keeper remains alive, and releases keeper afterward. No historical backend PID is signaled.

Copy hashes alone never establish complete input. Acceptance additionally requires the actual logger's pipe-EOF/flush record, expected schema-creation/admin sessions, immutable backend/session linkage, contiguous log records, positive controls and lifecycle boundaries. Missing expected evidence is failure, not no-DROP proof. Logs show attempted SQL; they do not by themselves show transaction commit.

## Required files

- `source.txt`: exactly two lowercase40-hex lines, actual commit and tree.
- `settings.txt`: unique `name=value` output from pg_settings. Required settings are logging_collector=on, log_destination=jsonlog, log_statement=all, log_directory=/tmp/process-failure-pg-log, log_filename=evidence.log, log_rotation_age=0, log_rotation_size=0, log_truncate_on_rotation=off, log_connections=on, log_disconnections=on, log_timezone=UTC, log_min_messages=debug1, log_line_prefix='PROCESS_FALLBACK %p %c ', lc_messages=C, log_error_verbosity=default.
- `container.json`: actual Docker inspect array. Its first object's Id must equal collector.container. State must report not Running, ExitCode0 and not OOMKilled.
- `initialization.json`: exact pid, start_ticks, collector, ready, reaped, exit and fresh_logs keys. Initial PID is integer>1, ticks positive integer, collector=off, ready/reaped/fresh_logs=true and integer exit=0. The initial PID differs from both final processes and its start ticks are no later than final postmaster start ticks. The keeper validates direct-child PID/start ticks, exec-to-postgres, matching PGDATA pidfile and explicit owned socket readiness, then owner-run normal stop and bounded direct-child wait0. No hook, existing PGDATA or earlier evidence directory is allowed.
- `collector.json`: container (64 lowercase hex), postmaster and logger process snapshots, stop_started_ns, logger_exited_ns, archive_completed_ns, logger_exit, logger_after and archive_sha256. Snapshots have positive integer pid/start_ticks, parent, state, exit_code and integer start_code/end_code. Same-postgres-UID reads must expose an actual live code range 1<start_code<end_code, not masked1/1. Initial process states are R/S/D/I with integer exit_code=0; postmaster.parent=1 and logger.parent equals postmaster.pid. Every identity and parent field is a positive integer; both final PIDs exceed the keeper PID1. Monotonic integer boundaries are positive and strictly ordered. logger_exit must be absent with logger_after=null. Transient zombies are polled without accepting their exit_code; persistent zombies time out. EOF plus disappearance proves drained input and no remaining collector, not its numeric exit status. archive_sha256 covers the exact server.tar bytes. Manifest construction is source-reviewed collection evidence, not an arbitrary declaration supplied by a test.
- `server.tar`: complete Docker directory archive. File members are exactly process-failure-pg-log/evidence.json and process-failure-pg-log/evidence.log. One optional directory member named process-failure-pg-log is allowed. Duplicate names, other directories, links and special files are rejected.
- `server/`: exactly the same two regular files. evidence.json is complete newline-terminated JSON Lines; evidence.log must contain exactly three newline-terminated lines: `PROCESS_FALLBACK <postmaster PID> <postmaster session_id> LOG:  ending log output to stderr`, then the same prefix plus `HINT:  Future log output will go to log destination "jsonlog".`, then `PROCESS_FALLBACK <logger PID> <logger session_id> DEBUG:  logger shutting down`. Official PG17.11 emits the startup LOG/HINT after SysLogger_Start before switching DestDebug to DestNone; logger EOF is also written to both destinations. All other bytes are rejected. Initialization uses the same official entrypoint and owned volume with collector disabled; its exec-final postmaster is positively identified, normally stopped and reaped before the captured final server starts. No temporary initialization collector contributes to this directory.
- `log-inventory.txt`: sorted sha256sum lines for both extracted files, matching the archive bytes.
- `green.json`, `success.json`, `red.json`: complete go tool test2json streams with Package=api.
- `bootstrap.log` and `bootstrap.json`: preserved actual-child output and exact reaped/exit metadata described below.

## Go event contract

Allowed actions are start, run, output, pass and fail. The package has one start and one terminal. Every test has one run and one terminal; output is inside its active lifecycle. Subtests run and end inside their active parent. Duplicate/unknown actions, missing terminals, skip, pause/cont and post-terminal output are not accepted for these nonparallel selected tests.

Green requires passing package plus seven roots: TestRecruitCleanupFailureGuard, TestRecruitCleanupFailureRunner, TestRecruitFailureOwnershipRejectsIncomplete, TestRecruitFailureAbsenceRequiresReap, TestPGRecruitFailureAbsenceRejectsLiveBackend, TestRecruitPanicAbsenceRejectsInvalidIdentity and TestPGRecruitCleanupFailureProcess. Guard and Runner each require fatal/goexit/panic/return subtests. Process requires original_fatal, original_goexit, original_panic, spare_fatal and raw-close_fatal subtests. No additional test terminal is accepted.

Success requires only passing TestPGRecruitGenerationConstructorCleanupPanic and package, with its existing verified primary/live/unknown/retained slot output. Red requires failing TestPGRecruitCleanupFailureProcess, original_fatal subtest and package, plus forbidden inherited fixture cleanup executed output. Race, test-timeout or build-failure diagnostics are not valid green/red witnesses.

## Bootstrap protocol

bootstrap.log contains exactly one each of RECRUIT_CLEANUP_FAILURE_POINT bootstrap:fatal, RECRUIT_CLEANUP_FAILURE_EXIT panic=<nil>, and RECRUIT_CLEANUP_FAILURE_BARRIER guard. Reject ownership or successful-witness prefixes RECRUIT_CLEANUP_PANIC_, FORBIDDEN_CLEANUP, race warnings, failure barrier release errors/timeouts, Go timeout panic and skipped-test diagnostics. bootstrap.json requires reaped=true (boolean), exit=1 (integer) and a cleanup-unverified result. In process_bootstrap database there must be exactly one actual CREATE SCHEMA attempt and no DROP SCHEMA attempt. The server must contain the single PROCESS_BOOTSTRAP_REAP_ABSENT SQL marker produced only after actual child reap and observed zero backends in that owned database. Its server record must follow the bootstrap CREATE and precede the end control; eventual disconnect callbacks need not precede it.

## Server and process-event contract

PG17 JSON records carry PID, session_id, session_start and line_num. session_start is UTC seconds derived from the same underlying start timestamp as pg_stat_activity.backend_start. Preserve full query-derived microseconds in APP evidence. Unique PID/normalized-second matching is corroboration and must identify the exact logged session, not an unrelated same-PID session. Session PID/start/database remain stable. Every process_* database session starts at line1 with connection received, has one authorization, retains its database after authorization and ends with disconnection. All retained session line numbers are contiguous.

The complete log contains exactly one startup redirect record with LOG severity, postmaster backend_type and the exact jsonlog hint. It binds to the recorded final postmaster and the same session as its unique readiness and shutdown; redirect precedes readiness, which precedes the begin positive control. The complete log contains startup readiness, bracketing PROCESS_LOG_begin/end SELECT+CREATE+DROP positive controls, and the exact postmaster's database system is shut down record followed by the recorded logger's logger shutting down DEBUG1 pipe-EOF/flush record. All test-database statements lie inside the positive-control interval. A DROP error statement is not silently normalized into success.

Each process case emits three RECRUIT_FAILURE_EVENT JSON observations in its exact Go subtest, and matching SELECT 'RECRUIT_FAILURE_SQL <JSON>' statements. Cases are unique timestamp-mode values; modes match the five green checkpoints or red original:fatal. Fields are Case, Stage, Database, Observer{PID,Start}, Owned{Schema,Original,Spares,Verified}, Barrier, Live, SchemaLive and ExitCode. Stage order is barrier-observed, reaped-backends-absent, case-end. Observer/Owned/Live/Barrier/Database/SchemaLive are stable across stages; ExitCode moves from -1 to1. SQL and output inventories are exactly bijective, including duplicates and unexpected protocol SQL.

Every case has exactly one earlier CREATE SCHEMA for its quoted owned api_return_<digits>_"Q schema on a distinct fully accounted admin session. Observer and each owned original/spare identity match distinct logged sessions; aliases across any roles are forbidden. The observer match is the marker session and remains live through case-end. Owned sessions have eventual complete disconnect records. A retained Live=true backend must disconnect after the barrier. Live=false and SQL absence do not imply earlier disconnect logs: PostgreSQL clears backend status before its disconnect callback. The actual child Wait/reap and exact PID/backend_start absence queries in the reviewed harness, followed by the same-observer SQL marker, establish the gate rather than callback log ordering. The parent DROP is exactly on that observer session after reaped-backends-absent and before case-end. Green has no other DROP, retains the schema at the guard barrier, and has a live original except at raw-close; all emitted spares are live. Red has one additional admin DROP on the CREATE session before the cleanup barrier while the immutable original is still live. Unaccounted DROP statements are rejected.

Original#2183 stays blocked until final source, parser, independent conformance and orchestration reviews, official ordinary/race PG evidence, original success, unchanged full API252/27/9 and all required CI pass. No production settings, permissions, deployment or guessed-schema cleanup follow from this contract.
